@@m8@@
Part 8

Forming your own view: both sides of every argument

Both sides of every live argument, so you can hold an opinion and defend it.

How to hold an opinion in a KKR interview@@d-how@@

KKR's EMEA client relations advert asks for the "ability to form and express opinions" [S388] CONFIRMED. This part gives you ten live arguments, both sides with numbers, and a defensible place to stand on each.

A good interview opinion has four parts: a view, one fact that anchors it, the best point against it, and what would change your mind. It does not need to agree with KKR. It needs to show you have weighed both sides INFERRED. The map below shows where KKR, regulators and critics roughly sit on each argument.

Why this matters

Notice that KKR sits on the left of almost every row. That is natural: it is a seller of these products. Your value in an interview is to show you understand why the right-hand side exists, and how a client team answers it honestly INFERRED.

1. Is private wealth "democratisation" good for retail investors?@@d-wealth@@

Yes: the case for

  • Individuals hold about 50% of global assets but only 16% of alternative fund assets [S293] REPORTED. Excluding them from an asset class that big firms use is its own unfairness.
  • Regulators on both sides of the Atlantic agree: EO 14330, the DOL safe harbour, the SEC accredited investor proposal, ELTIF 2.0 and the LTAF all widen access [S273, S272, S275, S301, S305] CONFIRMED. SEC Chair Atkins: "financial sophistication can scarcely be measured by income or net worth alone" [S275] REPORTED.
  • ELTIF assets grew 55% in 2025 to about €34bn [S302] REPORTED: demand is real.

No: the case against

  • In Q1 2026 investors asked for $20.8bn back from private credit funds; managers paid "just over half" [S337] REPORTED. Retail investors met the gate.
  • Apollo Debt Solutions received requests of 11.2% and paid 5% [S278] REPORTED.
  • The IMF lists semi-liquid vehicles and stale valuations among private credit vulnerabilities [S287] REPORTED; the FCA found weak valuation governance in 2025 [S310] REPORTED.
  • PitchBook: evergreen growth "funnels more capital into the hands of the largest GPs" [S260] REPORTED. Good for them; not automatically for savers.

KKR's position appears to be: strongly for. K-Series grew to $42bn [S330] CONFIRMED; Nuttall said the turbulence "has not changed our perspective on investing in growth" [S362] REPORTED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "Good for retail investors if the product is sold as what it is: semi-liquid. The gate is the product working, not failing. The risk is in the selling, not the structure." Anchor fact: K-FIT received requests for 6.3% in Q1 and paid about 80%; in Q2 requests fell to 1.65% and were paid in full [S338] REPORTED.

2. Is private credit a bubble?@@d-credit@@

Yes: the warning signs

  • Jamie Dimon after JPMorgan's $170m Tricolor loss: "when you see one cockroach, there are probably more" [S280] CONFIRMED.
  • Tricolor (Chapter 7, Sep 2025) and First Brands (over $10bn of liabilities, alleged double-pledging of invoices; moved to liquidation in Aug 2026) [S282, S283, S284] REPORTED.
  • The IMF warned vulnerabilities "could become systemic" [S287] REPORTED. The Bank of England is running a private markets stress scenario worse than the 2008 crisis; final report due early 2027 [S288] REPORTED.
  • Software is 64% of one Blue Owl BDC [S279] REPORTED, at a time when AI threatens software borrowers.

No: the defence

  • Apollo argues private credit is a market of "over $40 trillion", mostly investment grade, with only about $2tn of levered lending [S285] REPORTED (critics say the usual definition is $1.7tn to $3tn [S286]).
  • "Underlying loan performance remains largely stable despite the outflows" [S337] REPORTED. BlueBay's Mark Dowding called Tricolor "corporate fraud rather than an underlying symptom" [S281] REPORTED.
  • Closed-end private debt funds had a 24.1% distribution rate and record 2025 net cash flow of $39.5bn [S260] REPORTED.
  • Private debt is the only strategy where fundraising grew: up 14.0% in the 12 months to June 2026 [S260] CONFIRMED.

KKR's position appears to be: not a bubble. Nuttall expects "a record third-party credit fundraising year" and said software is "about 6% of our AUM" [S362] REPORTED. KKR runs $331bn in credit and liquid strategies [S332] CONFIRMED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "Not a system-wide bubble, but an asset class whose growth has run ahead of transparency. The fraud cases were about collateral checks, and the redemption wave was about software exposure. Underwriting and disclosure are the tests, not size." Anchor fact: Q1 2026 redemption requests were $20.8bn, driven by software worries, while loan performance was reported "largely stable" [S337] REPORTED.

3. Will the fundraising drought end?@@d-drought@@

Yes: signs of thaw

  • PE fundraising topped $260bn in H1 2026, a pace 17% above 2025 [S336] REPORTED.
  • Average time to close fell to 15.7 months from 19.1; 82% of PE funds closed at or above target, the highest in six years [S266] CONFIRMED.
  • 2025 buyout deal value rose 44% and exit value 47% (Bain) [S262] CONFIRMED. Exits refill LPs' pockets.

No: still dry

  • Total private capital raised in the 12 months to June fell 12.7% to $1,348bn; if the pace holds, 2026 is the fifth straight annual decline [S260] CONFIRMED.
  • Only about 310 PE final closes in H1, on track for the lowest count in over a decade [S336] REPORTED; 7,739 funds still on the road [S266] CONFIRMED.
  • Distributions were 6% of AUM against a 2015-19 average of 16% (McKinsey) [S261] REPORTED. McKinsey calls the shifts "structural features of a maturing industry" [S263] REPORTED.

KKR's position appears to be: for KKR, there is no drought: "We expect a record fundraising year for the firm" [S362] REPORTED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "It has already ended for the largest platforms. For the rest of the industry it ends only when distributions recover, because LPs fund new commitments with cash returned from old ones." Anchor fact: distributions at 6% of AUM against a 16% pre-2020 average [S261] REPORTED.

4. Does scale win?@@d-scale@@

Yes: flight to scale

  • Funds above $1bn took 78.2% of capital in H1 2026, up from 59.1% in 2021 [S260] CONFIRMED. The ten largest funds closed in Q2 took 49% [S266] CONFIRMED.
  • Only 36 first-time PE funds closed in H1 2026, raising $7.7bn [S260] CONFIRMED.
  • Allocators prefer "GPs with established track records and broad market validation" over the cost of underwriting smaller funds [S260] CONFIRMED.
  • Consolidation: BlackRock bought GIP and HPS [S290]; Nuveen bid $13.5bn for Schroders; over 1,500 asset manager deals forecast to 2029 [S291] REPORTED.

No: limits of size

  • Bain's "12 is the new 5": deals now need about 12% annual EBITDA growth, against about 5% historically [S262] REPORTED. Big funds must deploy big cheques in that world.
  • KKR's own house view says manager selection matters more when results diverge [S360] CONFIRMED: size is not the same as skill.
  • Concentration raises the stakes of each relationship: lose one LP and you lose several mandates INFERRED.

KKR's position appears to be: a beneficiary. Two of the year's largest closes (NAX4 about $23bn; GII V $19.2bn) [S335, S334] CONFIRMED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "Scale wins the fundraising, but it does not guarantee the returns. The client team's job is to show the scale is earned: breadth across strategies, co-investment, and service no small manager can match." Anchor fact: 78.2% of capital to $1bn+ funds in H1 2026, against 59.1% in 2021 [S260] CONFIRMED.

5. Should UK pensions be pushed into private assets?@@d-ukpensions@@

Yes: the growth case

  • The Mansion House Accord: 17 providers covering about 90% of active DC savers pledged 10% in private markets by 2030, 5% in the UK, potentially £50bn [S315] CONFIRMED.
  • Chancellor Reeves: "we are choosing to back British businesses and British workers" [S315] CONFIRMED.
  • A May 2026 Isio study found master trusts "rapidly increasing" illiquid allocations [S348] REPORTED: the pledge is already moving money.

No: the member's case

  • Trustees' first duty is to members. The Act lets them opt out if compliance is "likely not to be in the best interests of members" [S346] CONFIRMED.
  • Parliament fought over it: the Bill went through "extended ping-pong" and mandation was limited to Accord levels [S316] CONFIRMED.
  • Delivery is slow: the LGPS missed its 31 March 2026 pooling deadline [S347] REPORTED. "I expect any move to internally managed funds to take time, especially in the area of alternatives" [S347] REPORTED.

KKR's position appears to be: no direct public statement found in the sources. KKR's UK investments (Norfolk Vanguard offshore wind, DCC) suggest it sees UK assets worth owning [S357, S356] INFERRED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "Encourage, do not mandate. The Act gets the design about right: a reserve power capped at the voluntary levels, not usable before 2028, with a members'-interest opt-out." Anchor fact: any mandation is capped at 10% of the default fund, no more than 5% UK, and lapses at end-2032 if unused [S346] CONFIRMED.

6. Are insurer-owned asset managers a good model?@@d-insurance@@

Yes: patient money

  • Insurers collect premiums and need long-dated assets; managers originate long-dated private credit. The match is natural [S285] REPORTED.
  • It creates "perpetual capital" that never has to be handed back on a fixed date: $334bn at KKR, up 16% [S330] CONFIRMED. That makes fees steadier.
  • Apollo argues most private credit is investment grade [S285] REPORTED.

No: hidden risks

  • The IMF warned that insurers have "significantly expanded" holdings of private credit and illiquid assets, citing multiple layers of leverage and stale valuations [S287] REPORTED.
  • Critics say the "$40 trillion" figure counts almost everything non-traded [S286] REPORTED.
  • The same group originates assets and buys them for its own insurer: a conflict to manage and disclose INFERRED.

KKR's position appears to be: committed. Global Atlantic, its insurance company, had $220bn of AUM at 30 June 2026 [S330] CONFIRMED, and Capital Group will manage part of Global Atlantic's fixed income [S363] REPORTED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "A strong model for funding, with a governance question attached. Independent valuation and clear disclosure of the conflicts are what make it defensible to clients and regulators." Anchor fact: KKR's perpetual capital of $334bn [S330] CONFIRMED, set against the IMF's warning on stale valuations [S287] REPORTED.

7. Evergreen funds: is the liquidity mismatch a flaw?@@d-evergreen@@

An evergreen fund owns illiquid loans or companies but lets investors ask for money back every quarter, usually up to about 5% of the fund. When requests exceed the cap, everyone gets paid a pro-rata share. The chart shows how that played out in 2026.

Not a flaw: it worked

  • Caps exist precisely so a fund never has to sell assets at fire-sale prices INFERRED. AIFMD II now requires at least two liquidity tools for EU open-ended funds [S295] CONFIRMED.
  • Blackstone's BCRED paid 100% of record Q1 requests of 7.9% [S278] REPORTED; K-FIT paid in full in Q2 [S338] REPORTED.
  • The model keeps growing: about $500bn in semi-liquid vehicles [S267]; US evergreen PE AUM rose from $51.3bn to $99.3bn [S260] REPORTED.

A flaw: the queue is the product

  • More than $11bn left private credit funds over two quarters; the US Treasury convened regulators on private credit liquidity [S278] REPORTED.
  • Blue Owl Capital Corporation II ended quarterly redemption offers in February 2026 [S278] REPORTED.
  • Partners Group's shares fell as much as 18.2% in a day on redemption news [S339] REPORTED.

KKR's position appears to be: the model is sound; Nuttall: "What you don't read about in the articles is the inflows" [S362] REPORTED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "The mismatch is the design, not the flaw. The flaw appears when a semi-liquid fund is sold as if it were liquid. So the fix sits with the client team: set expectations at the point of sale." Anchor fact: closed-end private debt funds kept a 24.1% distribution rate while evergreen vehicles were "battered by outflows" [S260] REPORTED: same assets, different promises.

8. Will AI change fundraising and investor relations?@@d-ai@@

Yes: a big shift

  • Client work is document-heavy: KKR's KCS intern advert lists due diligence requests, RFPs, portfolio statistics and pitch decks [S390] CONFIRMED. First drafts are what AI does well INFERRED.
  • KKR's London client relations advert asks for "Strong working knowledge of AI-enabled productivity tools ... use generative AI effectively and responsibly" [S388] CONFIRMED. KKR's internship text encourages interns "to leverage KKR's approved AI tools" (KKR posting, quoted in this pack's brief) REPORTED.
  • Tailoring one message to many audiences is a core skill in the same advert [S388] CONFIRMED; AI makes versioning cheap INFERRED.

No: limits that matter

  • Every client document must be approved: the US Marketing Rule, UK Consumer Duty and EU pre-marketing rules do not accept "the model wrote it" [S313, S308, S299] INFERRED.
  • Confidential and inside information cannot go into unapproved tools INFERRED.
  • Kravis: "Our business really runs on trust" [S384] CONFIRMED. Trust is built person to person.
  • AI is also a portfolio risk: worry about AI-disrupted software borrowers drove the Q1 redemption wave [S337] REPORTED.

KKR's position appears to be: pro-adoption with controls ("approved" tools, used "responsibly") [S388] CONFIRMED; its house view sees a productivity boom, with "more of this improvement ... now in the price" [S361] CONFIRMED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "AI takes the first draft of the DDQ answer, the meeting brief and the market summary. Humans own the relationship, the judgement and the compliance sign-off. That frees juniors to spend more time on the client, not less." Anchor fact: KKR asks London analysts to "use generative AI effectively and responsibly" [S388] CONFIRMED.

9. The founders' control sunset: good for KKR?@@d-sunset@@

Yes: a normal public company

  • By 31 December 2026 KKR will "cancel the Series I preferred stock, establish voting rights for all common stock on a one vote per share basis, and acquire control of the carry pool" [S332] CONFIRMED.
  • Shareholders approved three charter changes on 21 April 2026 [S350] CONFIRMED, and 86.60% of outstanding shares backed removing the 90% supermajority rule [S351] CONFIRMED: clear support.
  • Leadership has already passed to co-CEOs Joseph Bae and Scott Nuttall [S330] CONFIRMED.

The open questions

  • The supermajority proposal still failed because it needed 90% [S351] CONFIRMED. Some protections remain.
  • Directors were elected by KKR Management LLP on 29 May 2026, as the current bylaws allow [S352] CONFIRMED.
  • The founders' culture ("one compensation pool", "like and trust") was built under founder control [S385, S384] CONFIRMED. Keeping it is a choice, not an automatic result INFERRED.

KKR's position appears to be: planned and supportive; the Sunset Date is written into its filings [S332] CONFIRMED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "Good for shareholders and neutral to positive for LPs. The real test is whether the one-firm culture and single compensation pool survive, because that is what clients buy." Anchor fact: the Sunset Date falls "no later than December 31, 2026" [S332] CONFIRMED.

10. The DPI drought: are continuation vehicles the answer?@@d-dpi@@

Yes: a new liquidity channel

  • GP-led secondaries reached $65bn in H1 2026, up 35%; single-asset continuation vehicles (CVs) were the largest share, "concentrated in high quality assets" [S267] CONFIRMED.
  • Evercore: secondaries are evolving "from an episodic liquidity solution into a structural portfolio management channel" [S267] CONFIRMED.
  • The backlog is huge: about $5tn sits in funds seven or more years old, 39% of NAV [S260] REPORTED; about 32,000 unsold companies worth $3.8tn [S262] CONFIRMED.

No: conflicts and fake exits

  • In a CV the GP sits on both sides of the sale. ILPA's draft guidance targets process integrity, conflicts and pricing validation [S319] REPORTED.
  • The SEC's rules on adviser-led secondaries were vacated in June 2024 [S311] CONFIRMED, so protection rests on ILPA and side letters INFERRED.
  • CVs grew 62% in 2025 but were still under 10% of exit value [S262] CONFIRMED. And about two-thirds of LPs would rather wait for a better MOIC than take liquidity now [S262] CONFIRMED.

KKR's position appears to be: building in. The Arctos deal created "KKR Solutions", home to "a scaled multi-asset class secondaries business" [S355] REPORTED; Q2 was KKR's "strongest monetization quarter ever" [S330] CONFIRMED.

Your opinion goes here

Suggested stance: "CVs are a useful tool, not a substitute for real exits. LPs should judge each one on process: independent pricing and a genuine choice to sell or roll. Exits like USI still do more for DPI than any CV." Anchor fact: CVs were under 10% of exit value in 2025 even after growing 62% [S262] CONFIRMED.

Delivering an opinion under pressure@@d-deliver@@

Say this in the interview

"My view is that semi-liquid funds are good for wealth clients if they are sold honestly. The best point against me is the Q1 redemption wave: $20.8bn of requests and only about half paid. What would change my mind is if gates became permanent rather than temporary."

Don't say this

"Private credit is definitely a bubble" or "private credit has no risk." Absolute claims invite a follow-up you cannot win. Also avoid "KKR is always right": the interviewer wants judgement, not loyalty INFERRED.

Why this matters

The same four-step structure (view, fact, best counter-point, what would change your mind) is what a client team does in front of an LP who asks a hard question. Practising it here is practising the job INFERRED.

@@m9@@
Part 9

The interview: process, question bank, questions to ask

How KKR London is likely to interview across all six teams, what each team tests, 75 questions as scaffolds, and ten questions to ask back.

You rank six teams on one application. Each team is likely to test you differently. This part gives the whole-programme view: the shared funnel, then each team's style and its own questions, then a general bank that every interviewer can draw from. The Client Solutions deep dive (in the separate KCS pack) goes further on that one team.

The shared funnel, then six branches@@m9-funnel@@

Every candidate likely goes through the same early stages. The split comes at the final round, where each team sets its own task. KKR's head of talent acquisition told Fortune that candidates "typically" meet 6 to 8 executives, including the hiring team's managing director or partner [S393] REPORTED.

Source uncertain

There is almost no public report of KKR's London summer internship interviews, through SEO London or otherwise. The process below is assembled from Fortune's reporting on KKR's US campus hiring [S393], commercial prep sites [S394] [S395] [S397] [S407] (medium to low reliability), anonymous forum posts [S401] to [S406] (anecdotes), and KKR's own London job adverts [S388] [S391] [S390] (primary). Treat team formats as likely, not certain.

StageWhat to expectPreparation that works for every team
Online testCognitive test of nearly an hour (US) [S393] REPORTED. "Criteria-style" aptitude test for some London roles [S394] REPORTED, low confidence.Two timed practice tests. SEO London trains psychometric tests [S374] CONFIRMED.
HireVue"Pre-set behavioral prompts with one attempt per answer" [S394] REPORTED. 3 to 5 questions is an unsourced estimate [S395].Record yourself answering the motivational and behavioural questions in this part. Watch it back once.
First roundOne or two live interviews, behavioural, technical and CV [S394] REPORTED. US anecdote: "Hirevue, 1st round zoom, 2nd round zoom (3 interviews), in-person superday (4 interviews)", 30 minutes each, analyst to MD [S402] REPORTED, anecdote.The general bank below, plus a crisp answer to "why this team?" for your top two.
Final round3 to 5 interviews (Leland) or 4 to 6 (Extern), plus a team task [S394] [S395] REPORTED. A last round with partners or division heads on long-term thinking and fit [S394] REPORTED.The team-specific sections below.

How each of the six teams interviews@@m9-teams@@

The grid below summarises what each team's interview is likely to lean on. It is a judgement from the reported formats, not a measured score.

Why this matters

Fortune's report lists what KKR recruiters look for: real interest in KKR specifically, how your background adds to the team, familiarity with recent deals and milestones, and an understanding of how the macro environment affects investors [S393] REPORTED. Those four apply to every team. The team tasks only decide how the technical part is tested.

1. Private Equity (including Global Impact)

What is reported. LBO or modelling tests at the final round; paper LBOs; deal walk-throughs; "what makes a good LBO candidate" [S394] REPORTED. Extern claims a 60 to 90 minute blank-sheet three-statement LBO, pass or fail [S395], unsourced. Leland says PE in the Americas uses a 2 to 3 hour in-person LBO case with no internet [S394] REPORTED. Glassdoor posters describe "basic live cases" comparing two hypothetical businesses [S402] REPORTED, anecdote. London intern format: unknown.

What it tests. Accounting fluency, LBO logic, investment judgement, and whether you can talk about a deal. London context. KKR's European Fund VI had $7,513m of commitments in the June 2026 10-Q, with a reported $8bn close in April 2023 [S175] [S185]. Recent European growth deals include Fresha in London ($80m at a $1bn valuation, May 2026) [S183] CONFIRMED. Global Impact Fund II had $2,709m of commitments [S175] CONFIRMED.

Key term

Paper LBO: a leveraged buyout done in your head or on paper in a few minutes. Example with illustrative numbers: buy a company with EBITDA (operating profit before depreciation) of 100 at 10x, so the price is 1,000. Borrow 500, put in 500 of equity. Five years later EBITDA is 200, sold at 10x for 2,000, and half the debt is repaid, so 250 is left. Equity is now 1,750, which is 3.5x the money (MOIC), roughly a 28% a year return (IRR). This question pattern is reported by a low-reliability site [S396]; the numbers are invented for teaching INFERRED.

PE questionScaffold
Walk me through an LBO. What makes a good LBO candidate? [S394]Price, debt and equity, cash flow pays debt, exit. Good candidate: steady cash flow, low capex, room to improve, sensible price.
Here are two businesses. Which is the better PE investment? [S402]Compare growth, margins, cash conversion, competition, cyclicality, price. Pick one and say what would change your mind.
Here is a company description: what are the three biggest risks? [S396]One market risk, one operating risk, one financing risk. Say how you would test each.
Depreciation rises by $10 and the tax rate is 25%: what happens to net income? [S395]Net income falls by $7.50; cash rises by $2.50 via lower tax. Walk through each statement.
Why private equity rather than investment banking? [S403]Ownership and long-term judgement, not "better hours". Tie to a KKR example.
Pitch a deal you would invest in. [S396]Business, why now, how value is created (operations, not only leverage), risks, exit. KKR's mid-year outlook tilts to "operational improvement, not financial engineering" [S360].

2. Real Estate

What is reported. A London RE analyst (full-time, interviewed 2022) described headhunter vetting, technical questions, a modelling exercise with debrief, then a three-interview superday over about two months [S401] REPORTED, anecdote. KKR's 2027 London RE off-cycle advert stresses "Strong financial modelling skills" and "Demonstrable interest in Real Estate" [S391] CONFIRMED.

What it tests. Property cash flows and valuation, modelling, and real passion for the asset class. London context. KKR's European logistics platform Mirastar bought UK logistics assets from PLP (about £170m, July 2026) and from Ares funds (September 2026) [S184] CONFIRMED. KKR formed a joint venture of up to £500m with Puma Property Finance for UK living-sector lending (March 2026) [S184] CONFIRMED. Global real estate: 120+ professionals and about $84bn of AUM (March 2026) [S142] CONFIRMED.

RE questionScaffold
How would you value a property? INFERREDNet operating income divided by a cap rate; check with comparables and a discounted cash flow. Explain each term.
Why logistics, and what could go wrong? INFERREDE-commerce and supply chains drive demand; risks are oversupply and tenant quality. Use the Mirastar deals [S184].
What does a rise in interest rates do to property values? INFERREDHigher financing cost and higher required yields push values down unless rents rise. Mention inflation-linked leases.
Equity or debt: where is the better risk-reward in European real estate now? INFERREDDefine both, give a view, cite KKR doing both (equity platforms and the Puma lending JV) [S184].
Tell me about your interest in real estate. [S391]A specific building, street or sector you have studied, not "I like buildings". This is the advert's own ask.
Walk me through your model. [S401]If a modelling test is set, the debrief matters: assumptions first, then outputs, then what you would check with more time.

3. Infrastructure

What is reported. No public interview report for KKR infrastructure was found [Gap]. Expect a PE-style process with questions on long-life assets, contracted cash flows and inflation linkage INFERRED.

London context. Global Infrastructure Investors V closed at $19.2bn on 3 August 2026, KKR's largest infrastructure fund, investing mainly in North America and Western Europe [S334] [S176] CONFIRMED. KKR manages about $120bn of infrastructure equity, up from $13bn in 2019 [S334] CONFIRMED. European deals: a 50:50 JV with RWE on the Norfolk Vanguard offshore wind farms (January 2026) [S181]; 50% of a €1.8bn TotalEnergies renewables portfolio, funded by "an insurance account managed by KKR" (August 2026) [S180]; more equity into European data centre platform Global Technical Realty [S182]. All CONFIRMED.

Infrastructure questionScaffold
What makes an asset "infrastructure"? INFERREDEssential service, long life, high barriers to entry, often contracted or regulated cash flows.
Why do investors want infrastructure now? INFERREDInflation links, steady income, and KKR's "Security of Everything" theme (energy, data, supply chains) [S360].
What is Core+ and how does it differ from a buyout? [S334]Lower risk, steady income plus some growth, lower target return than buyouts. GII V is a Core+ fund [S334].
Offshore wind: what are the main risks? INFERREDConstruction cost, power prices, grid connection, policy. Mention the RWE JV and that capex is over $15bn [S181].
Why are data centres an infrastructure asset? INFERREDLong contracts with large tenants, power-hungry, essential to AI demand. Helix Digital Infrastructure launched June 2026 with $10bn+ [S3].
How would higher rates affect an infrastructure valuation? INFERREDHigher discount rate lowers value; offset if revenues are inflation-linked. Show both sides.

4. Capital Markets (KCM)

What is reported. A prep site describes about four rounds, with debt financing and LBO capital structures, market views or a pitch idea, and a case on capital structure or debt capacity [S407] REPORTED, low reliability. An older leveraged-credit anecdote: "how would you value a company" [S407].

What it tests. Debt basics, capital structure, and market awareness. London context. Mark Danzey is European Head of KCM, Global Co-Head of Debt Capital Markets and European Head of Institutional Client Solutions [S156] CONFIRMED. KKR's UK capital markets LLP had 10 employees and 10 members in 2025 [S172] CONFIRMED. KCM earned $930m of transaction fees in 2025 [S70] CONFIRMED. KCM began in 2007 to raise the amount of third-party capital KKR could commit to deals [S208] CONFIRMED.

KCM questionScaffold
Why would KKR have its own capital markets team rather than use banks? [S208]Control over financing, speed, fees kept in the firm, ability to syndicate to clients. Note Blackstone and Apollo also have one [S214] [S220].
Walk me through a typical LBO capital structure. [S407]Senior secured loans, high-yield bonds or private credit, equity. Explain seniority and cost.
How much debt can this company carry? [S407]Start from EBITDA and a sensible leverage multiple; check interest cover; consider cash-flow stability.
Bank loan, bond, or private credit: when would you use each? INFERREDSpeed and certainty (private credit), cost and size (bonds), flexibility (loans).
What is syndication? [S70]Committing to a large financing or equity cheque then selling parts to other investors. KCM syndicates co-investments to clients [S70].
Give me a market view. [S407]One trend in credit markets, with data. KKR's outlook calls credit technicals "more supportive" [S360].

5. Client Solutions (KCS)

What is reported. For a KKR Client Solutions associate role, a prep site lists a recruiter screen, a first round, a possible "Case Study/Writing Exercise" of 1 to 2 hours and a final round [S397] REPORTED, low-medium. KKR's London KCS adverts ask for the ability to "tailor messages to suit different audiences", "Technical and aesthetic mastery of PowerPoint and Excel", and responsible use of generative AI [S388] CONFIRMED. Full treatment is in the KCS pack, Part 9.

What it tests. Explaining products and markets, writing, attention to detail, client service.

KCS questionScaffold
Why Client Solutions rather than an investment team? [S397]What you enjoy (explaining, relationships, seeing the whole firm), plus evidence. KCS "seeks to 'connect the dots' across all businesses at KKR" [S390].
Explain DPI to a new investor. [S398]Cash returned divided by cash paid in. LPs watch it closely because distributions have been low [S262].
What is a capital call? [S397]The fund asking investors for part of their promised money when a deal is found.
Evergreen versus drawdown funds? INFERREDNo end date and periodic, capped redemptions versus a fixed-life fund that calls money over years. K-Series reached $42bn [S73].
Pitch a KKR fund to a UK pension in two minutes. INFERREDClient need, product, why KKR, two risks, next step. GII V is a strong example [S334].
Write a two-paragraph update for investors. [S397] [S399]What happened (two numbers, a date); what it means for the reader, one risk, what comes next.

6. Capstone

What is reported. Glassdoor: three 30-minute interviews, a CV and behavioural one first, then a "high-level case with simple mental math" on improving a company's metrics [S405] REPORTED, anecdote. Fishbowl: fit plus cases plus an analytical test "cutting raw data rather than building a financial model" [S406] REPORTED, anecdote, older.

What it tests. Structured problem solving, quick numbers, and practical business sense. Context. KKR's 10-K describes "operational guidance from our operating professionals at KKR Capstone" [S174] CONFIRMED. Capstone fees were $113.6m in 2025 [S201] CONFIRMED. London has 15 Capstone bios at Principal level and above, the same as London PE [S149] CONFIRMED; Juan de Ochoa, Partner, is co-head of Capstone EMEA [S161] CONFIRMED.

Capstone questionScaffold
A company's margins are falling. How would you find out why? [S405]Split revenue (price, volume, mix) from costs (materials, labour, overheads); find the biggest mover first.
How would you improve this company's EBITDA by 10%? [S405]Revenue levers and cost levers; size each one with quick maths; pick the top two.
Here is a table of raw data: what does it tell you? [S406]Sort, group, look for outliers; state one insight and one question. Do not over-model.
Quick maths: 15% of 340? Cost falls 8% on a 60% cost base: margin change? INFERRED51. Costs fall 4.8 points of revenue, so margin rises by 4.8 points. Say your steps aloud.
Why operations rather than deal-making? INFERREDYou like fixing things you can see. Tie to "operational improvement, not financial engineering" [S360].
Tell me about a process you improved. INFERREDBefore, what you changed, measured result. Credit the team.

General question bank: 42 scaffolds any interviewer could use@@m9-bank@@

These cut across teams. Each row gives a scaffold (the order of points), not a script. Tags: a source ID means the question is reported there; INFERRED means strongly implied but not seen as a real question. CV walk-through and live scenarios are covered in other parts of this pack.

Motivational (7)

#QuestionScaffold
1Tell me about yourself. [S394] [S419]Now, two formative chapters, why this room. 60 to 90 seconds. End on the team you ranked first.
2Why KKR? [S394] [S402]Structure, milestone, culture, each with "which matters to me because". Fails the test if it would fit any other firm [S414].
3Why this team? [S402] [S419]What the team does in your words, what draws you, evidence you would be good at it.
4Why private markets / alternatives? [S398] [S399]Long-term ownership, real assets and companies, relationships that last a decade. Avoid "pay" and "hours".
5How did you rank the six teams, and why? INFERREDOne-line logic, then a real reason for choice two. Consistency matters more than the order.
6Where do you see yourself in five years? [S394]Skills and responsibilities, not titles. Show you would stay and grow.
7What kind of professional do you want to become? [S394]Two traits and the habits you are building to get there.

Firm knowledge (7)

#QuestionScaffold
8What do you know about KKR? INFERREDFounded 1 May 1976 with $120,000 [S13]; $796bn AUM at 30 June 2026 [S74]; asset management, Global Atlantic insurance, strategic holdings [S1]; one-firm culture.
9Tell me about a recent KKR deal. [S393] [S394]What, why, risks, what you would watch. Pick one you can defend for five minutes.
10How has KKR changed since its founding? INFERREDTraditional PE was over 70% of AUM in 2010 and under 25% now [S2] [S332]; credit, infrastructure and insurance grew.
11How is KKR different from Blackstone or Apollo? INFERREDSay where KKR is smaller (total AUM, wealth, insurance) [S213] [S220]; then what is distinctive: one compensation approach, KCM tied to client work [S3].
12What does "like and trust" mean to you? [S384] [S386]Trust is earned by doing what you say. Your own example. Optionally Walter Industries [S384].
13What is the "one firm" model and why does it matter? [S385]One compensation pool, single expense pool [S70]; people share ideas and clients. Lewin: "Relationships travel, ideas travel" [S3].
14What is KKR's view on the economy right now? [S394]McVey's Mid-Year 2026: "the cycle continues, but the rules of the game are changing"; divergence; quality and durable cash flows [S360].

Industry and markets (7)

#QuestionScaffold
15How is the macro environment affecting investors? [S393]One force (inflation, rates, geopolitics), effect on investors, what it means for KKR.
16How will auto loans perform in the current economy? [S404]A London 2023 question. Method: consumer health, rates, used-car prices, lending standards. Give a view.
17Why has it been hard for PE firms to sell companies? INFERREDValuation gaps, financing costs, IPO windows. Bain counts about 32,000 unsold companies worth about $3.8tn [S262].
18Is private credit a bubble? INFERREDBoth sides: Q1 2026 redemption requests of about $20.8bn [S337]; underlying loan performance reported "largely stable" [S337]. Your view.
19Why does AI matter for private markets? INFERREDDemand side (data centres, power) and risk side (software exposure, about 6% of KKR's AUM) [S362].
20What do UK pension reforms mean for firms like KKR? INFERREDPension Schemes Act 2026 [S346]; LGPS pooling [S347]; fewer, bigger buyers.
21What market trend are you following? [S394]Trend, data, winners and losers, how you track it. Be ready for a follow-up.

Technical (8)

#QuestionScaffold
22Walk me through the three financial statements. [S403]Income statement to net income; net income starts the cash flow statement; cash and retained earnings link to the balance sheet.
23What are the main valuation methods? [S394]Comparable companies, precedent transactions, discounted cash flow; when each fits.
24What discount rate would you use? [S403]The cost of capital that matches the risk of the cash flows (WACC for a firm). Explain why riskier means higher.
25How would you value a company? [S407]Ask what kind of company, then pick methods and cross-check. Show judgement, not just formulas.
26IRR versus MOIC. [S399]MOIC: how many times your money; IRR: how fast. Both matter, plus DPI for cash returned.
27What is EBITDA and why do investors use it? INFERREDProfit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; a rough proxy for operating cash flow. Know its limits (capex).
28What is enterprise value versus equity value? INFERREDEV is the value of the whole business; equity value is what is left for shareholders after net debt.
29How do fees work in a private fund? INFERREDManagement fee, carried interest, hurdle. Terms vary; large LPs negotiate.

Behavioural (7)

#QuestionScaffold
30Describe a time you led a team through a difficult situation. [S394]Situation, task, actions (mostly), result with a number, lesson. "We" for the team, "I" for your actions.
31Describe a team project. [S395]Your role, a problem, how you helped others succeed. KKR values thinking "in terms of 'we', not 'I'" [S389].
32Tell me about a time you disagreed with a team. [S396]Listen, evidence, outcome, relationship afterwards.
33Tell me about a time your judgement was wrong. [S394]Own it in sentence one, fix, habit built. Arrogance fails KKR's test [S385].
34Describe a time you communicated complex information simply. [S397] [S399]Audience, confusion, new explanation, proof it worked.
35How do you keep accuracy high under deadlines? [S397] [S398]Your system, one example, an error you caught.
36How have you used AI tools responsibly? [S388]Task, tool, how you checked, what you would not delegate. KKR's internship text encourages its "approved AI tools" (brief).

Curveballs (6)

#QuestionScaffold
37What would you have done differently on our last deal? [S394]Admit what you cannot know from outside; ask a clarifying question; offer one hypothesis with a reason.
38How do you think about risk? [S394]What can go wrong, how likely, how bad, what you control. A personal example.
39What is the best decision you made that turned out badly? [S384] INFERREDJudge the process, not the outcome. Kravis calls a bankruptcy his "best deal" [S384].
40What is the impact of [today's headline] on the economy? [S403]Name the channel (prices, rates, confidence, trade), the sectors hit, what you would watch.
41What would you change about KKR? INFERREDRespectful, evidence-based, framed as a question. Avoid scandal-hunting.
42Teach me something in two minutes. INFERREDA topic you know well, an analogy, one number, a check-for-understanding question.

Conduct on the day, whichever team you face@@m9-day@@

KKR's founders say they judge "who the person is", not only skills [S385] CONFIRMED. Most of that judgement happens between the questions. The checklist below applies to every team and every stage INFERRED.

Before

  • Re-read your own application. Interviewers often start from what you wrote INFERRED.
  • Know three current numbers: AUM $796bn at 30 June 2026, $34bn raised in Q2, K-Series $42bn [S330]. After 9 November, update them from the Q3 release [S333].
  • One-line answers ready for "why KKR", "why this team", "why your ranking".
  • For video: camera at eye level, quiet room, notes out of shot. HireVue gives one attempt per answer [S394].

During

  • Answer first, then explain. Interviewers have 20 to 30 minutes [S402] [S403].
  • For a technical question you cannot answer: say so, then reason aloud from what you do know. Guessing a number is worse than a clear "I don't know, here is how I would work it out" INFERRED.
  • Ask to write things down in a maths or case question. It is normal and shows care INFERRED.
  • Use "we" for team results and "I" for your own actions.

Everyone counts

  • Kravis: KKR watches how candidates treat people they are not trying to impress; "Those who are arrogant fail this test" [S385] CONFIRMED. That includes reception, SEO staff, IT support on a video call and other candidates.
  • Be on time and do what you say. "Our word is our bond" [S384] CONFIRMED.

After

  • Note every question you were asked within an hour. Patterns help in the next round INFERRED.
  • If you send thanks, keep it short and specific to one point from the conversation. Send it only through the channel the recruiters used INFERRED.
  • Do not post interview questions online; treat the process as confidential INFERRED.

Ten questions to ask back@@m9-ask@@

Pick one or two per interview. Match the question to the person: practical ones for analysts and associates, strategic ones for MDs and partners. The KCS pack has a further ten for Client Solutions.

#QuestionWhy it lands
1"KKR's mid-year outlook favours operational improvement over financial engineering. How does that show up in how your team underwrites a deal?"Links the house view [S360] to their daily work. Works for PE, Infra, Capstone.
2"The TotalEnergies renewables deal was funded by an insurance account managed by KKR. How often does Global Atlantic capital now sit beside fund money in European deals?"A detail from the press release [S180]; shows you see the insurance link.
3"With KKR opening in Milan and Abu Dhabi, how much is the London team's role changing from covering Europe to supporting local offices?"Uses recent office news [S169] [S184]; relevant to any London team.
4"KKR says it runs one compensation approach. How does that change how teams share work with each other day to day?"Grounded in Lewin's words [S3]; invites a story.
5"In European real estate, KKR is active in both equity and lending, for example the Puma living-sector JV. How do you decide which side of the capital structure to be on?"RE-specific, recent [S184].
6"KKR's European Head of Capital Markets also heads Institutional Client Solutions. How does KCM work with the client team on co-investment?"KCM or KCS; shows you read bios [S156].
7"How does Capstone get involved before an acquisition, as well as after?"Capstone; probes the operating model [S174] without assuming the answer.
8"What does a strong intern on this team produce by the end of the summer?"Works with anyone; shows you think about adding value.
9"Which piece of KKR Insights do people on your team find most useful, and why?"Shows you read KKR's research [S394] [S360].
10"What is something about working at KKR that surprised you when you joined?"Personal-professional, safe, invites a real answer. Never ask about private life.
Don't say this

"KKR is the biggest private equity firm." By total AUM it is behind Blackstone ($1.35tn) and Apollo ($1.05tn) at $796bn [S213] [S220] [S200] CONFIRMED. "KKR is the only firm with in-house capital markets." Blackstone and Apollo have them too [S214] [S220] CONFIRMED.

Part 10

Interviewer briefing

Who is likely to interview you, how to read them in two minutes, the senior names worth knowing, and a 20-minute routine for when real names arrive.

No interviewer has been named yet. This part prepares you for the types of people you will meet and the handful of senior names every KKR London candidate should recognise. It uses public professional information only: job titles, teams, career paths and public statements. Nothing personal, and no tactics designed to manipulate anyone.

Who typically interviews@@m10-who@@

TypeWhere you meet themEvidenceConfidence
SEO London staffBefore KKR: application support, shortlisting, interview guidance, logistics.SEO tells sponsor firms its "delivery team can support you with shortlisting" [S371]; its Alternatives programme offers "Interview guidance" [S372].CONFIRMED that the service exists; INFERRED that it applies to KKR in 2026
KKR campus recruitersScreens, scheduling, possibly a first call; present on the day.KKR's Student Careers page refers to "KKR's Campus Recruiting Team" [S370]. KKR's head of talent acquisition spoke to Fortune in 2024 [S393]. A recruiter screen is listed for a KCS associate process [S397]; a "phone screening" in an intern anecdote [S419].REPORTED
Junior practitioners (analysts, associates, principals)First rounds and parts of the superday.First rounds with associates or principals [S394]; interviewers ranging from analyst to MD [S402] (anecdote).REPORTED
Senior practitioners (directors, MDs, partners)Superday and final round.Candidates "typically" meet 6 to 8 executives, including the hiring team's MD or partner [S393]; final round with partners or division heads [S394].REPORTED

For Client Solutions specifically, the London team at Principal level and above has about 20 listed people [S149] CONFIRMED, so a KCS candidate may well meet someone from that list. The directory lists only Principal level and above, so analysts and associates who interview you will not appear there [S149] CONFIRMED.

Reading the interviewer in the first two minutes@@m10-read@@

You are not trying to "work" the interviewer. You are trying to pitch the depth and length of your answers at the right level, the way a good client professional would INFERRED. Three honest signals tell you most of what you need:

  1. How they introduce themselves. A title and team ("I'm an associate in Infrastructure") tells you seniority and practitioner status. A recruiter usually introduces the process first INFERRED.
  2. Their first question. "Walk me through your CV" or a values question suggests a fit screen. A technical or market question suggests a practitioner testing depth INFERRED.
  3. How they react to your first answer. Follow-ups on detail mean "go deeper"; moving quickly on means "shorter answers" INFERRED.
Don't do this

Mirroring body language on purpose, flattering the interviewer, guessing at their politics or private life, or changing your story to suit them. These are manipulation tactics, they are easy to spot, and they clash with KKR's stated test of "like and trust" [S384] INFERRED. Adapt depth and length; never adapt the truth.

When names arrive: a 20-minute research routine@@m10-names@@

Recruiters sometimes share interviewer names a day or two before. Spend no more than 20 minutes per person. The aim is one relevant, professional point of connection and the right pitch level, not a dossier INFERRED.

MinutesDoWhy
0 to 4Find the person's bio on kkr.com ("Our People"). Note title, team, city and how long they have been at KKR.Primary source; confirms identity and seniority, which tells you which box of the 2x2 they sit in.
4 to 8Search KKR's press releases and media centre for their name: deals, fund closes, appointments, promotions.Gives you one recent professional fact, for example a fund they helped raise [S184] [S165].
8 to 12Check whether they have authored or spoken in public: KKR Insights, conference panels, interviews.Public views you can respond to thoughtfully if the topic comes up.
12 to 15Look at their professional profile only (role history). Do not send connection requests or messages before the interview.Career path context. Contact before the interview can look like lobbying INFERRED.
15 to 18Write one question for them that links their team's public work to your interest. Use the question lists in Part 9.Turns research into a genuine question, not a recital.
18 to 20Write down the pitch level (2x2 box) and one identity check (is this definitely the same person?).Avoids the embarrassment of confusing two people with the same name.
Why this matters

The point of the routine is relevance and respect. One light reference ("I saw your team's infrastructure fund closed in August") shows homework. A list of facts about the person reads as surveillance and breaks the "like and trust" test [S384] INFERRED.

Fair game
  • Job title, team, city, years at KKR.
  • Deals, funds and initiatives they are publicly linked to.
  • Their published articles, talks and quoted statements.
  • Prior employers and roles listed on their KKR bio.
Off limits
  • Family, home, health, religion, politics, age.
  • Personal social media, photos, hobbies not shared professionally.
  • Anything found by digging beyond professional sources.
  • Contacting them, their colleagues or their assistants to gain an edge.

Part 11

The scenario playbook: frame method, ladder, composure set, CV grill

One method for any "what would you do?" question, a fixed priority order, 30 practice scenarios across all six teams, five composure tests and a CV drill.

Every KKR team asks some version of "what would you do if...?". The question tests judgement, honesty and calm more than knowledge. This part gives you a short method, then drills it on the general intern duties and on each qualification the internship asks for, with scenarios set in Private Equity, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Capital Markets (KCM), Capstone and Client Solutions (KCS). The KCS deep dive has a fuller version for client roles.

How to read this part

The protocol, priority order, counters and drills are method: our advice, not KKR facts. Scenarios are invented for practice. Facts inside them carry source IDs and confidence tags. KKR does not publish its scenario questions. What is known: candidates "typically" meet 6 to 8 executives [S393] REPORTED, and Henry Kravis says KKR looks "beyond financial acumen" for "like and trust" [S385] CONFIRMED.

The method: protocol, priority order, one sentence@@m11-method@@

The four-step protocol (45 to 75 seconds)

The priority order when good things collide

Method. Hard scenarios set good against good: helping your MD against fairness, speed against sign-off. Decide the order now, so you never invent it under pressure. For any KKR intern role:

The one sentence that holds every frame

"I would get it right, keep it fair, write it down, and then make it fast." Say it to yourself whenever pressure scrambles your thinking. Method.

Why this order. Kravis: "Our business really runs on trust. People don't want to work with you, let alone entrust you with their capital, if they can't trust you will do what you say" [S384] CONFIRMED. Fairness between investors is policed: in 2015 the SEC found KKR had misallocated more than $17m of broken-deal costs to its flagship funds rather than sharing them with co-investors, and KKR paid nearly $30m [S20] CONFIRMED. Records matter: in January 2025 KKR paid $11m in an SEC sweep over business messages sent on unapproved apps [S29] REPORTED. Investment committees "review and evaluate investment opportunities using frameworks that are designed to include qualitative and quantitative assessments of the key investment risks" [S2] CONFIRMED, so a hidden risk is a process failure as well as an accuracy one INFERRED.

Eight frame breakers and the counters@@m11-counters@@

Method. Interviewers push on purpose to see whether you fold. The rule for all eight: acknowledge the pressure, keep the order, offer a better option.

Staying calm physically

  • Rehearse out loud, timed, with a phone stopwatch. Rehearsed answers feel short in the room.
  • One slow breath out before Step 1; feet flat, hands still.
  • Write two words on your pad when the question lands ("speed / accuracy"). It anchors Sort.
  • Slow your pace, not your volume. Pauses read as thought.
  • If you blank: "Can I take five seconds to order my thoughts?" Nobody marks that down.
  • Be kind to everyone in the building. Kravis says KKR watches how candidates treat people they are not trying to impress [S385] CONFIRMED.

The ladder: three scenarios for each duty and qualification@@m11-ladder@@

Ten lines, three rungs each: easy (do you understand it?), medium (two good things collide) and hard (pressure plus a twist). Lines 1 to 4 are the general intern duties; lines 5 to 10 are the testable qualifications. Each scenario is set in a named team so you practise across the whole programme.

Where these lines come from

Every duty and qualification line here is quoted from KKR's own 2027 London internship description, as published on the SEO London listing and the attached team descriptions [Advert]. The core sentence reads: "summer interns will be involved in helping identify attractive investment themes and opportunities, synthesizing industry and market data and analysing potential investments. Interns are encouraged to leverage KKR's approved AI tools to accelerate their work, deepen their learning, and contribute fresh perspectives on how emerging technology can enhance the way we operate." The SEO application form itself sits behind a login and was not read [S392].
